source.title: Scaling Adaptive Depth with Norm-Agnostic Residual Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies model depth-to-width ratio at approximately fixed parameter counts and reports training loss, bearing on V4's claim about architecture shape and loss. It does not test the power-law scaling or compute-optimal allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss comparisons across depth-to-width ratios, which bear on V4. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute, fit scaling laws, or test downstream predictability. Other reported results on MoD, attention sinks, geometry, and weights do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study trains five baseline MoE Transformers at fixed forward-pass (~150M) and total (~900M) parameters and fixed tokens (50B). Only the width-to-depth ratio varies (80 to 20; hidden size 1408 to 928, 18 to 40 layers). It reports final loss for each, which bears directly on V4. Fixing the parameter count and varying shape is close to the original ablation design. The measure is training loss, not held-out loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that NAG lowers training loss over matched baselines, with gains growing in deeper models, because it controls residual-stream norm growth. They add that NAG enables a geometry-based Mixture-of-Depths that beats router MoD and that, at about 20–25% skipping, matches full-depth loss under iso-FLOP pretraining.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares NAG and baseline architectures across depth-to-width ratios; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law measurement or fit procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported NAG advantage grows with depth and begins to saturate at the deepest tested configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: In iso-FLOP runs with fixed total parameters, Mixture-of-Depths skipping lowers active forward-pass parameters and adds tokens. Loss stays nearly flat up to 20% MoD (+0.00055) and rises to +0.01854 at 40% (Table V).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under fixed training compute, reallocating forward-pass compute to more tokens via depth sparsity leaves loss nearly unchanged at moderate sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: The NAG residual architecture lowers training loss by about 0.012–0.028 relative to baseline. The gain grows with depth, so the effect of shape interacts with the residual-stream design (Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The influence of depth/width shape on loss depends on residual-stream normalization design.

record.problems: The reported loss comparison is training loss rather than held-out loss. Exact losses are presented only in a figure, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. The architecture sweep is limited to one model family and approximately fixed parameter counts.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results omitted. The downstream benchmark, MoD, geometry, weight-distribution, and attention-sink results were excluded because they do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Only depth/width aspect ratio is tested, at one scale (150M active / 900M total MoE), one data budget and one optimizer (Muon). Other details such as heads and feed-forward ratio, and other sizes, are not tested.
No scaling of loss with parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested. Downstream evals are reported but not related to scale.

missing.what: A numeric baseline and NAG loss at ratio 60 (2.35539 and 2.33661), usable as values for r3 and r4
Per-ratio baseline-minus-NAG loss differences printed above the Fig. 2 bars (0.01176, 0.02849, 0.01893, 0.02202, 0.02186). The mapping to ratios is ambiguous in the extracted text.

record.verdict_notes: V4 evidence comes only from the baseline arm of the aspect-ratio ablation. The NAG rows are the study's own method vs baseline and should not carry V4. Losses are training losses, figure-only except for ratio 60, with no uncertainty reported. Across ratios the baseline spread is roughly ≤0.04 nats (under 2% of loss), consistent with 'shape matters little'. The authors themselves stress the mild depth trend and attribute saturation to width becoming a bottleneck.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
The loss-minimising parameter/token split as a function of fixed compute.
Tests depth-to-width ratios in one MoE Transformer setup; does not isolate all architecture details or establish effects across model sizes and training settings.
Power-law forms in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, or departures from single power laws.

relationships.condition: Baseline pre-norm MoE Transformers, ~150M forward / ~900M total params, 50B Zyda-2 tokens, width-to-depth ratios 80–20
relationships.reason: Across a 4x range of aspect ratio, baseline training losses stay within the 2.32–2.36 band of Fig. 2 (BASELINE-60 = 2.35539). There is only a mild deeper-is-better trend that saturates at the deepest setting (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Training losses stayed within 2.32–2.36, with a mild advantage for greater depth that saturated at the deepest setting.

labels.condition: Baseline pre-norm MoE Transformers, ~150M forward / ~900M total params, 50B Zyda-2 tokens, width-to-depth ratios 80–20
labels.reason: The condition group is tested, but support remains unverified: Figure 2's extracted axis ticks do not establish the asserted loss range. The text reports improvement and saturation without quantifying cross-shape absolute differences.

relation.reason: The study measures losses across parameter-matched depth and width configurations, providing its own results relevant to V4.

tranche.reason: The controlled architecture ablation bears directly on V4 using a different experimental setup and final training loss.

source_check.notes: Figure 2's missing bar heights limit verification of V4; this is not evidence against it. The authors' summary is broadly faithful, although 25% MoD is suggested rather than directly tested.

statements.correction: Width-to-depth ratios=80,60,40,30,20; approximately 150M forward-pass and 900M total parameters; 50B Zyda2 tokens; Muon optimizer; no-MoD BASELINE-60 loss=2.35539; loss generally improves with depth and begins to saturate in the deepest configurations; other absolute baseline losses are figure-only.
statements.problem: The MoE configuration and training conditions are supported. Figure 2 retains tick labels from 2.32 to 2.36, but its bar heights are missing; tick endpoints alone do not establish that all baseline losses fall within that interval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MoE Transformer models with approximately 150M forward-pass and 900M total parameters, at tested model ratios 80, 60, 40, 30, and 20
reader_labels.reason: Training loss generally improves as models become deeper, and NAG's gain over baseline increases with depth before beginning to saturate; this indicates some dependence on depth/width shape, but the paper does not give extractable values to assess whether the change is only slight (r1-r10).
